questions.q: Explain the philosophy of the Indian Constitution as reflected in its Preamble.
answer: The Preamble is the soul of the Constitution and sums up the philosophy and ideals on which India is founded.

answer.text: It declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic. Sovereign means India is free of external control, socialist that it aims at reducing inequality, secular that the state treats all religions equally, democratic that power flows from the people, and republic that the head of state is elected.

The Preamble promises to secure to all citizens justice, social, economic and political; liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality of status and opportunity; and fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation.
Together these express a vision of a free, just and equal society, making the Constitution an instrument of social transformation.

answer: Thus the Preamble captures the guiding philosophy of the Constitution.

questions.q: How do the values of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble shape the Indian Constitution?

answer.text: sets out the guiding values of the Constitution — justice, liberty, equality and fraternity — which shape the whole document.

list: Liberty guarantees freedom of thought, expression, belief and worship, reflected in the Fundamental Rights
Equality assures equal status and opportunity, reflected in the abolition of untouchability and equal protection of the law

answer.text: It gives the values a common purpose.

list: Fraternity means a sense of brotherhood among all Indians and respect for the dignity of the individual
Together these values, drawn from the freedom struggle, are the moral compass of Indian democracy
